why_these_three: These three are fixed forever. Changing them would silently reset the baseline and every comparison made against it, so a later job that wants a different question adds a fourth rather than swapping one out.

No exact_verse or exact_quotation question is here on purpose. A bare citation like 'BG 18.66' takes the pinned-lookup road with no five-angle plan and no real fan-out, so it measures a cheaper pipeline than the one we are trying to make faster, and would flatter every later job.
The three differ in shape so that a change which helps one and hurts another is visible instead of averaging out.

questions.question: How do I control my mind?
questions.role: The clean middle case: short, ordinary, gets a full five-angle plan.

questions.question: Compare karma-yoga and bhakti-yoga
questions.role: The plain topic phrase with no question mark. A devotee who omits the punctuation is still asking, and this must still earn five angles rather than being read as a pointer. A repeated ROLE across its angles is legitimate here, because comparing two things means defining both.

questions.question: I have been trying to chant regularly for about two years now but my mind keeps wandering during japa and I often feel that I am simply going through the motions without any real attachment, so what did Srila Prabhupada advise for someone in this situation?
questions.role: What devotees actually type. Both live searches on record were this shape, and it exercises the long-query preprocessing path that the short questions never reach.

how_to_run.cold: One search of question 1 alone, after at least 30 minutes idle. That single run is the cold number.
how_to_run.warm: Then four rounds, each round being question 1, then 2, then 3, in order.
how_to_run.labelling: Only the first isolated run is genuinely cold. By the second question the shared indexes are already partly resident, so nothing else may be called cold.
how_to_run.reporting: Per question: the cold number once, and the MEDIAN of the four warm runs. Never average cold and warm together.
